submission.justification: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm is recommended as the choice that best balances the separation goal against the humidity-transparency hard constraint. Separation at 10 GeV/c from the simulation: R1 is highest (4.59 sigma at 3 cm; peak near 3 cm, 4.11 at 1 cm, 3.21 at 6 cm), R2 peaks at 3 cm (3.68 sigma; 3.34 at 1 cm, 3.63 at 2 cm, 3.51 at 4 cm, 2.79 at 6 cm), and R3 is weakest (2.13 sigma even at 6 cm). R1 offers about 0.9 sigma more separation at 3 cm, but it is a porous radiator without a hydrophobic treatment, and no project document provides its 10-year humidity ageing transparency. R2 is the porous candidate with a hydrophobic treatment, which is the design feature most directly aimed at humidity resistance. The transparency-loss requirement is NOT verified for R2 either: the simulation tool reports only separation, and no document gives ageing results. Before procurement, the 10-year humidity ageing test must be run on the R2 tiles at 3 cm to confirm loss is at most 10%. If R2 fails that test, R3 (solid) is the fallback, and R1 should only be chosen if its ageing data show at most 10% loss.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is candidate 2 (porous with hydrophobic treatment).

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing must not exceed 10% (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No project document gives ageing or transparency-loss data for any candidate, and the simulation tool reports only separation. Compliance for R2 is inferred from its hydrophobic treatment, not measured. Must be verified by ageing test before procurement.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R2 at 3 cm gives 3.68 sigma, below R1 at 3 cm (4.59 sigma). R2 was chosen for humidity robustness, which trades away about 0.9 sigma. R1 would be the separation-optimal choice only if its ageing transparency loss were verified at or below 10%.
